g2-implement.title: Close the unrendered-field class with a falsifiable completeness property: implement
g2-implement.imperative: Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md and dispatch a constellation-implementer subagent through scripts/run_crew.py. Task: make tests/test_checklist_engine.py's TaskFieldCompleteness able to FAIL for the shapes the corpus really carries. Five changes, all inside that class: (1) remove 'directives' from _EXCLUDED_FIELDS and replace its KNOWN GAP comment with the rendering note; every remaining exclusion keeps its stated per-entry reason. (2) Replace _flatten with a TOTAL leaf extractor that recurses dicts and lists to any depth and stringifies scalars, returning [] only for None and empty containers -- this is what makes the nested-dict shape assertable at all. (3) Replace the single checked_any flag with a PER-FIELD ledger: record which fields the loop actually asserted on, then assert that set equals the set of populated non-excluded fields. A recursive extractor alone still reports green when a future field yields no text, because one flag for the whole loop lets any field cover for any other. (4) COLD-CRITIC FINDING 1, and this is the change that actually closes the class: the loop runs over the FIXTURE's keys, so a Task field added later and forgotten in the fixture is absent from the loop, absent from the ledger's expected set, and passes green -- the identical forgetting failure this property exists to catch. Assert the fixture's key set is a SUPERSET of the engine's own canonical Task builder _build_amend_task (scripts/checklist_engine.py:2040, mirrored by append() at :2252), so a field added to the engine's Task shape and forgotten here fails mechanically. State the residual limit honestly in the class docstring: a field introduced only by a template and never by either builder still needs a human to add it. (5) Add an in-suite NEGATIVE self-test that feeds the same assertion path a render with the directives block stripped and asserts it raises, naming directives. Then run the red-proofs by hand and paste the REAL output in the result: R2 make the extractor return [] for dicts -> expect the ledger set-mismatch, NOT a green run; R4 add a throwaway field whose value flattens to nothing -> expect it to fail by name; R5 add a field to _build_amend_task and not to the fixture -> expect the superset assertion to fail by name. Revert each break before the next. (R1, suppressing the renderer, is deliberately dropped: change (5) automates exactly that world.)
